To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
E. coli O157:H 7 strains can replicate and diversify in cattle, which may result in the emergence of new strains.
EHEC O 157 : H7 strains that were inoculated into calves underwent mutation and clonal turnover during their replication in the host.
The EHEC O 157:H7 strains used in our experiments were genetically different from the strains that were isolated from cattle.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular epidemiology of EHEC O 157:H7 strains isolated from experimentally infected calves.
the development of a molecular epidemiological tool for the detection of EHEC O 157:H7 clones in the bovine reservoir.
the molecular epidemiology of enterohemorragic Escherichia Coli (EHEC).

clonal turnover of EHEC O 157:H7 occurs in experimentally infected calves.

EHEC O 157: H7 strains are capable of clonal turnover in cattle and that the clonal turnover may be due to the loss of the inoculating strains and/or the emergence of new clones.

the EHEC clone that is inoculated into cattle is not necessarily the clone that is shed in manure.
